headline: 27 nations join ASSOCIO Digital & AI Summit 2026 in Jakarta
summary: The three-day international technology conference focuses on AI governance, cybersecurity, and regional cooperation in the Asia-Oceania region.
details: The Asian-Oceanian Computing Industry Organization (ASSOCIO) has launched its three-day international technology conference, 'ASSOCIO Digital & AI Summit 2026', in Jakarta, Indonesia.
Representatives from 27 out of 31 member countries are participating in the event, which is being held at the Swissôtel Jakarta PIK Avenue from Monday to Wednesday.
The summit features strategic discussions on digital transformation, AI governance, responsible AI, cybersecurity, and digital infrastructure, alongside a showcase of AI technologies.
ASSOCIO Chairman Stan Singh-jit of Malaysia emphasized that cybersecurity is now the foundation of economic stability and digital trust in the rapidly evolving digital world.

Abdullah H Kafi, ASSOCIO Life Chairman and former president of the Bangladesh Computer Society (BCS), noted that Bangladesh is lagging behind in the global AI race compared to countries like Indonesia and India.
A 15-member delegation from the Bangladesh Computer Society (BCS) is representing Bangladesh at the summit to expand business and institutional connections and exchange knowledge within the region.

headline: Hilsa prices rise Tk 250-300 per kg ahead of 22-day fishing ban
summary: Supplies of the national fish have declined compared to last year, pushing prices up as a fishing ban is set to begin on October 8.
details: A 22-day ban on hilsa fishing will begin on October 8, covering 38 upazilas in major rivers across Bangladesh. This has led to a decrease in supply, causing prices to rise by Tk 250-300 per kg over the past week.
In Barishal's wholesale markets, 1 kg hilsa is now selling for Tk 2,760, while smaller fish weighing 400-600 grams are selling between Tk 1,560 and Tk 2,130 per kg.
Production levels have dropped significantly. In the Barishal division, 41,134 tonnes were produced in September this year, compared to 49,790 tonnes during the same period last year.
Fisheries officials note that production in August was also lower this year, falling to 13,718 tonnes from 14,964 tonnes last year.
Enforcement of the ban may face challenges due to a shortage of fisheries officers in seven upazilas across Barishal, Patuakhali, and Bhola, as well as a lack of allocated funds for operations.
Over 500,000 fishermen in the Barishal division are struggling as they failed to catch the expected quantity of hilsa, increasing their debts.
To support them, the government has allocated 16,157 tonnes of rice for 646,290 fishermen nationwide, with each receiving 25 kg during the ban period.
caption:
Hilsa prices have jumped by Tk 250-300 per kg in just one week. Why is the national fish becoming more expensive?

A 22-day ban on hilsa fishing will begin on October 8, covering 38 upazilas in major rivers across Bangladesh. This has led to a decrease in supply, causing prices to rise by Tk 250-300 per kg over the past week.

In Barishal's wholesale markets, 1 kg hilsa is now selling for Tk 2,760, while smaller fish weighing 400-600 grams are selling between Tk 1,560 and Tk 2,130 per kg.

Production levels have dropped significantly. In the Barishal division, 41,134 tonnes were produced in September this year, compared to 49,790 tonnes during the same period last year.

Fisheries officials note that production in August was also lower this year, falling to 13,718 tonnes from 14,964 tonnes last year.

Enforcement of the ban may face challenges due to a shortage of fisheries officers in seven upazilas across Barishal, Patuakhali, and Bhola, as well as a lack of allocated funds for operations.

Over 500,000 fishermen in the Barishal division are struggling as they failed to catch the expected quantity of hilsa, increasing their debts.

To support them, the government has allocated 16,157 tonnes of rice for 646,290 fishermen nationwide, with each receiving 25 kg during the ban period.
